summary:
Vologda Oblast stands under the national framework of Russia. Its legal position on gender recognition, public expression and extremist designations is set by national law, and the source inventory contains no oblast-level statute, decree or enforcement programme that alters that position.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (June 2025) assesses Vologda Oblast at the national score and identifies no regional deviation. A trans visitor in the oblast consequently faces the same legal exposure as elsewhere in Russia, as set out in the Russia record.
tangentialFactors: The June 2025 Home Office note is the only source in this inventory that addresses Vologda Oblast, and it does so only to record the absence of regional deviation. No incident, court ruling, local ordinance or enforcement practice specific to the oblast appears in the inventory, so there is no adjacent regional material to weigh against the national assessment.
localsOnly: The source inventory contains no resident-facing information specific to Vologda Oblast: no oblast-level document rule, no regional service and no local protection mechanism is described. Residents live under the same national framework as the rest of Russia.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Home Office assessment is scored at the national level and publishes no oblast-level enforcement figures. No count of administrative fines, public-expression cases or extremism prosecutions in Vologda Oblast is available in this inventory.

Whether police and courts in Vologda Oblast apply the national provisions more or less intensively than agencies elsewhere in Russia is unresolved on the sources reviewed.
